A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Text Has Curvature by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original corpus-based holonomy/CEI measurements and LongBench pruning and routing results in Sections 4 and 7 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original corpus diagnostics and reports revised utility results, generator and extractor comparisons, curvature distributions, and relational analyses.

M1.justification: Section 5 replaces the bridge-midpoint free-energy score with activity-weighted transport contraction across rectangles of the two-sided belief field. This requires grid-wide beliefs, debiased Sinkhorn divergences, and holonomy/CEI gating. V2 also introduces CurvPrune-Hybrid and replaces signed transversal bridge curvature with nonnegative relational transport spread.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText-2, OpenWebText, and the same five LongBench tasks: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Qasper, GovReport, and QMSum. The suffix-swap and local-shuffle scenarios remain. New model comparisons and relational/distribution analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds actual Fixed-k retrieval results, with k=5 specified in Appendix E.6; v1 names this baseline but reports no corresponding scores. The other external comparators remain. LC is not newly introduced, since it already appears in v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: The reported main generator changes from Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. V2 adds evaluation configurations using Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, and four additional frozen extractor checkpoints. Its newly disclosed N=50 utility sample size does not establish a sample-size change from v1.

E4.justification: V2 adds reported generator/extractor robustness checks, Pure-versus-Hybrid pruning comparisons, surprisal correlation, signed curvature distributions and sentence cases, and relational-versus-longitudinal analysis. It supplies budget-sweep results and quantifies previously asserted stability. Figure 4 replaces the telescoping and frequency-rank diagnostics with joint-certificate and paired real-versus-swap analyses.

E5.justification: V1 utility tables report means with standard deviations and mark p<0.05 significance. V2 reports point estimates and replaces significance checkmarks with a practical threshold of at least one absolute point. Appendix E.3 adds an explicit discussion of large bootstrap uncertainty; the stated 95% confidence level and 1000 resamples remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Utility values and rankings are extensively replaced: HotpotQA BM25/BM25+Texture scores change from 27.3/27.0 to 28.1/38.4, while CurvFlag changes from 29.1 F1 at 148 tokens to 49.1 at 3344 tokens. The operator and generator also change, preventing interpretation as controlled across-version gains. V2 adds sweep, portability, extractor, and relational results; the original existence summaries in Tables 4–5 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 introduces transport-divergence, rectangle-contraction, and activity-aggregation definitions, with new boundedness, flat-rectangle, and contraction propositions in Appendix C.3. These replace v1's bridge-energy identities and factor-eight curvature derivation, and the continuity theorem is revised. The original holonomy/PoE proofs and bridge-existence theorem are retained under different numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the central contribution from midpoint-based contextual bridge curvature to bounded, signed two-axis Contextual Ricci Texture. The novelty statement is recast around an extractor-based, generator-agnostic primitive, and the abstract removes the explicit inference that non-flatness means language has inherent curvature.

C2.justification: V2 interprets focus/fan-out through contraction/expansion and explicitly discusses extractor-dependent magnitudes, cancellation at zero aggregate curvature, and the unsigned scope of the relational readout. It explains curvature-only pruning's weakness through missing query relevance and limits the strongest utility benefits to multi-hop QA. These materially refine the earlier interpretation and applicability claims.

D1.justification: V2 supplies additional concrete disclosures: N=50 utility samples, controller weights and hybrid mixing strength, the pinned reference-state rule, relational neighborhood/fusion parameters, and per-slot timings. It also states that per-example traces are released. The broader configuration-logging, caching, and code-release descriptions already existed in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds Feydy et al. on Sinkhorn divergences and dataset/generator references, removes Ambrosio et al., and changes positioning from an alternative to a complement to curved-model training. The related-work organization and most cited literature remain. Ollivier's corrected publication year represents the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, utility explanations, and results discussion undergo substantial rewriting around the new curvature interpretation. Experimental details move behind the theory and utility appendices, and v2 adds explicit limitations and conflict-of-interest text. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 are redrawn for the revised operator, Figure 4 is replaced, and Figures 5–12 add substantial new displays. Tables gain budget/model comparison structures, relative-effect columns, and colored ranking highlights. Existing results are also rearranged and restyled.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies the sweep results missing from v1's claimed sweep, tests generator/extractor generality, and clarifies important applicability limits. These strengthen empirical support and interpretation. The net gain is limited by reduced utility uncertainty reporting and incomplete theoretical updating: Theorem C.6 still assumes convergence of boundary beliefs without specifying convergence of the full field required by the revised operator.
